meta.title: "That's beside the point, but you…" — how children get steered off-topic in conversations | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to spot when someone dodges a question and bring the conversation back. Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: Does your child's question keep going unanswered?
hero.subheadline: She asked something direct — and got back "what about you yesterday…", "that's beside the point", "let's talk about something else". And never got what she actually asked for.

media.alt: A child hearing topic-deflection instead of an answer

pain.title: "That's beside the point, but…": when instead of an answer, you get steered elsewhere
pain.body:
"Why can't I go?" → "Who were you out with yesterday?". "That's not fair" → "What about Wednesday when you…". "Why are you shouting?" → "Let's talk about school instead". Your child asked one thing — and got answered on something completely different. The conversation drifted, and her question just hung in the air.

This isn't confusion or 'losing the thread'. It's a deflection — instead of answering, the other person redirects attention to a different situation, a different person, a different moment. The subject shifts so quietly that the child starts answering the new one. By the time she realises, she's forgotten what she originally asked.

The result — the question stays unanswered. The child walks away with a feeling of being 'outplayed' but can't even put her finger on how. Next time, asking will feel harder — she's already half-expecting to be steered elsewhere.

solution.body: 40 episodes, 13 critical thinking lessons. Your child plays — but is actually learning to hold a conversation on topic.

social_proof.quote: She used to sit there afterwards thinking 'what just happened'. Now she says: "Mum, that's not what we were talking about. Can you answer my question?" I sometimes catch myself dodging — and she notices now.
social_proof.author: Olena, mum of 10-year-old Alisa

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
